proof.text: Put $T=R\setminus\{0\}$ and $K=T^{-1}R$. In the fraction construction [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $a/t=0$ precisely when $ua=0$ for some $u\in T$, hence precisely when $a=0$, because $R$ is a domain. Every nonzero $a/t$ has inverse $t/a$, so $K$ is a field. Let $V=T^{-1}N$, a $K$-module, and let $i:N\to V$ send $n$ to $n/1$. If $i(n)=0$, the stated kernel criterion for module localization gives $tn=0$ for some $t\in T$; torsion freeness of $N$ gives $n=0$. Thus $i$ is injective. The restricted $R$-action on $V$ is the original localization action.

proof.text: The localization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] applied to $R\to K=T^{-1}R$ makes $K$ flat over $R$. The field-module lemma [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] makes the $K$-vector space $V$ flat over $K$, without any dimension bound. Transitivity [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive], with $(A,B,M)=(R,K,V)$ and the compatible scalar actions of Step 1, now makes $V$ flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), (1) and (2); flatness reformulation of the vector-space basis argument in more-algebra.tex, Tag 0AXM.

proof.text: The flat-map hypothesis means that $S$ is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] with its $(M,N,P,f)=(S,N,V,i)$ to obtain an injective map $J:S\otimes_R N\to S\otimes_R V$, $s\otimes n\mapsto s\otimes i(n)$. It is $S$-linear: on pure tensors $J(bs\otimes n)=bs\otimes i(n)=bJ(s\otimes n)$, and the identity extends by additivity and generation by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

By Step 2, $V$ is $R$-flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] to $R\to S$ and $V$: the target $S\otimes_R V$, with $S$ acting on the first factor, is flat over $S$. Since $S$ is a domain, [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] implies that multiplication by every $0\ne b\in S$ is injective on this target. This establishes torsion freeness for all nonzero target scalars, including those outside the image of $R$.

source.place: Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change); flat-target version of the localization/direct-sum argument concluding more-algebra.tex, Tag 0AXM.

proof.text: The bilinear formula $n\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes n$ defines $\tau:N\otimes_R S\to S\otimes_R N$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the reverse formula defines its inverse, since both composites are the identity on the generating pure tensors. Also $\tau(n\otimes bs)=bs\otimes n=b\tau(n\otimes s)$, so $\tau$ is $S$-linear for the stipulated second-factor action on the source. If $bz=0$ with $0\ne b\in S$, then $bJ\tau(z)=J\tau(bz)=0$. Step 4 gives $J\tau(z)=0$; injectivity from Step 3 and invertibility of $\tau$ give $z=0$.

title: Flat extension of domains preserves torsion-free modules
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative integral domains, and let $N$ be an $R$-module. Assume $N$ is torsion free: for every $0\ne a\in R$ and $n\in N$, $an=0$ implies $n=0$. Then $N\otimes_R S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $S$ acting on the second tensor factor, is torsion free as an $S$-module: for every $0\ne b\in S$ and $z\in N\otimes_R S$, $bz=0$ implies $z=0$. No finite generation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.
